heading: PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF BANTUL

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Government is the Central Government.
2. Region is Bantul Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency.
7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against victims.
10. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence.
12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance.
16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if there are restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights.
17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or sexually nuanced speech, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in discomfort, feeling offended, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems.
18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency.
19. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
23. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and mental health is achieved.
27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
28. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him civilly.
30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence.
31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
32. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
33. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers from perpetrators in accordance with predetermined standards.
34. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
35. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree.
37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency.
40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources.
41. Violence Victim Protection Forum hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against Children and Women whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

heading: Article 2
Article 3
CHAPTER II
Article 5
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

The obligations and responsibilities in organizing protection for children and women victims of violence are:
a. Regional Government;
b. society;
c. family; and
d. parents.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

The Regional Government shall organize services for victims in the form of:
a. facilitating the establishment of PPT;
b. facilitating PPT facilities and infrastructure according to capacity; and
c. facilitating FPKK as a network forum for victim handling.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to:
a. supervise the organization of services for victims in accordance with minimum service standards; and
b. provide funds for victim protection through the APBD.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

In implementing the obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in Article 7, Article 8, and Article 9, the Regent shall grant authority to the SKPD that has duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 11
Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letters c and d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

ORGANIZATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutions

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the main duties, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, consisting of fields.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.
4. PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.
5. In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence shall be referred to other institutions.

heading: Article 14
Article 15
Article 16
Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

The social rehabilitation service field as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2) letter c has the duties of:
a. providing assistance during the case handling process;
b. conducting counseling; and
c. carrying out social functions.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

The repatriation and social reintegration field as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2) letter d has the duties of:
a. conducting coordination with related agencies for victim repatriation;
b. preparing progress reports on the repatriation assistance and social rehabilitation process; and
c. conducting monitoring for a maximum of 3 (three) months after the victim is returned to their family.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

The legal aid service field as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2) letter e has the following duties:
a. accompanying and defending in every legal process; and
b. preparing reports on the progress of legal case handling.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

The spiritual field as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2) letter f has the following duties:
a. providing spiritual guidance to victims;
b. coordinating with related parties; and
c. preparing reports and recommendations for follow-up services.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

The psychology field as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (2) letter g has the following duties:
a. providing psychological guidance to victims;
b. preparing recommendations for follow-up services; and
c. coordinating and making referrals to follow-up services.

heading: Article 22
Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

The organizational structure of PPT established by the Regent involves related SKPD with community institutions adjusted to needs.

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

Further provisions regarding the development, mechanism and networked working relationship of PPT shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

FORMS AND MECHANISMS OF PROTECTION

Part One

Prevention

heading: Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

Prevention efforts shall also be carried out by:
a. the community;
b. families; and
c. parents.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Services

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
2. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

heading: Article 28
Article 29
Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

Complaint, consultation, and counseling services as referred to in Article 29 letter a include:
a. initial identification or recording of victims; and
b. consent to take action.

heading: Article 31
Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

Health services as referred to in Article 29 letter c include:
a. first aid to victims;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 29 letter d constitute services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems, by:
a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

Legal services as referred to in Article 29 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 29 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. other Regional Governments; and
b. related agencies and institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

Psychological services as referred to in Article 29 letter g aim to:
a. provide psychological accompaniment and services; and
b. provide psychological recovery of victims from trauma.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Empowerment

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

Forms of empowerment of women victims of violence include:
a. job training, including:
1. skills training;
2. field work practice; and
3. apprenticeship.
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups, including:
1. entrepreneurial skills training;
2. facilitation of the formation of joint business groups; and
3. business implementation assistance.
c. capital assistance, including:
1. assistance with work facilities and infrastructure; and
2. facilitation of working capital assistance.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Protection and Fulfillment of Children's Rights

heading: Article 38
Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. In an effort to guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights, the Regional Government cooperates with the Children's Forum that has been established.
2. The Children's Forum is an organization whose members are children who are administrators of children's organizations, studios or children's activity groups and the like, which are generally based on the development of talents, interests, abilities and use of leisure time.
3. The Children's Forum has the following duties:
a. conduct socialization about violence to peers;
b. actively participate in planning policies, programs and activities related to the protection of children from violence;
c. become a source of information on incidents of violence in their environment; and
d. consult the needs and desires of child victims of violence to partners from related sectors.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Coordination of Services and Protection for Victims

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

1. In an effort to provide and organize handling of services and protection for victims, PPT establishes FPKK.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of PPT services;
b. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on violence.
3. The management and membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by the Decision of the Chair of PTT.
4. The membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (3) is grouped into the following roles:
a. health role;
b. psychology role;
c. legal role;
d. social role; and
e. economic role.
5. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties, functions and membership of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP

Part One

Cooperation

heading: Article 41
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Partnership

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business world in the protection of children and women from violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. an information system on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for children and women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for children and women victims of violence who are vulnerable to dropping out of school; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of a joint agreement.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 44

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of PPT Minimum Service Standards.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

REPORTING

Article 43

1. PPT and FPKK prepare reports on the protection of Children and Women victims of violence to the Regent.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months and shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FUNDING

Article 45

1. Funding is provided by the Regional Government for activities to protect victims of violence and shall be charged to the APBD.
2. Management of funding allocation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the needs of PPT by coordinating between SKPDs.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 46

1. The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of violence.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the sub-district/village level by the community;
b. establishing Child and Women protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of the rights of Children and Women;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 47

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Bantul Regency.

on 20 NOVEMBER 2013

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY

NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

One of the purposes of establishing a state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is explicitly stated in the Preamble of the Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Paragraph IV. It is stated that the national goal of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and the entire Indonesian homeland, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice.

To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 of 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time.

This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is a manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will improve.

Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on Women; Convention of Elimination and Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through laws and regulations, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, as well as the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children.

It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the Convention on Women which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate gaps, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention on Women (articles 1-16).

Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents must understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of children are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of abuse, neglect, eviction and mistreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe and friendly place for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, clerics/religious leaders and networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The many cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish an Integrated Service Center and Violence Victim Protection Forum (FPKK) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main tasks and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence.

From the framework above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children. From these various efforts, a legal framework will be realized in the implementation of protection for children and women from violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of victims' rights.

Letter b
What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Letter c
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
What is meant by "the best empowerment for victims" is all recovery, rehabilitation, reunification actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the main consideration.

heading: Article 3
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 3

Paragraph (1)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Point a
What is meant by the "prevention" aspect is a protection strategy effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes conflict resolution without violence, stress management skills, resource management, effective decision making, effective interpersonal communication, guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.
b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur, what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress management training.

Point b
What is meant by the "service and assistance" aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Point c
What is meant by the "empowerment" aspect is the process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection of women and children broadly.

heading: Article 4
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 4

Point a
What is meant by "the right to have their dignity respected as human beings" is upholding human rights.

Point b
What is meant by "health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by victims" is assistance provided by health experts (doctors) for physical disorders suffered and from psychologists to victims who suffer from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition.

Point c
Sufficiently clear.

Point d
What is meant by "obtaining information" is access and information about the whereabouts of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments that contain values, meanings, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Point e
What is meant by "confidentiality of identity" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Point f
What is meant by "optimal service" is service that includes medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.

Point g
What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.

Point h
What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop until physical and psychological healing, legal assistance to restore civil rights, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of good name, and citizenship.

Point i
What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Point j
Sufficiently clear.

Point k
What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious leaders, advocates, and family members. Meanwhile, legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and during the legal process.

Point l
Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 15
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 15

What is meant by "conducting interviews and observations of victims" is if the victim's condition has begun to recover from trauma and it is possible to conduct interviews. Meanwhile, what is meant by observation is knowing the environmental context, role and status when acts of violence occurred against the victim.

heading: Article 24

translated_text:
Article 24

Paragraph (1)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Point a
What is meant by "network" includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups in the community. What is meant by "coordination" includes: planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs.

Point b
What is meant by "violence prevention system" includes: mapping locations or areas prone to violence and conducting promotive and preventive efforts to the community.

Point c
What is meant by "Critical education about the rights of children and women" is an effort to build awareness of children and women about their rights. The purpose of implementing critical education is to be able to help decisions and not become victims of repeated violence. Forms of critical education for the community consist of: training on gender equality and justice, education on reproductive health for women, and providing understanding of laws and regulations on the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Child Protection.

Point d
Socialization can be carried out through mass media, electronic media, and direct counseling to the community.

heading: Article 25
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 25

Point a
Prevention efforts in the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members.

Point b
Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, seeking to eliminate provisions that do not side with victims of violence.

Point c
Prevention efforts in the community include: fostering environmental awareness of acts of violence that occur in their environment.

heading: Article 27

translated_text:
Article 27

Letter a
What is meant by "no fees charged" is that the activities of service provision and assistance carried out by PPT are not charged to victims from underprivileged families.

Letter b
What is meant by "prompt" is immediate action taken without complications or with simplified procedures.

Letter c
What is meant by "safe and comfortable" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly, respectful and appreciative manner.

Letter d
What is meant by "empathy" is action that respects, honors, cares for, befriends, and brings happiness with the aim of pleasing and comforting the victim's heart.

Letter e
What is meant by "non-discrimination" means not making distinctions for any reason or in any way, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.

Letter f
Sufficiently clear.

Letter g
What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively adequate for the privileged.

Letter h What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to provide certainty to victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Letter b

What is meant by "medicolegal" is medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medicolegal services include, among others: visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum.

What is meant by "visum et repertum" is a written statement made by a doctor in forensic medical science at the request of an authorized investigator regarding the results of a medical examination of the victim based on their expertise and under oath, for the purposes of judicial proceedings.

What is meant by "visum et psikiatrikum" is a statement given by a Psychiatrist regarding the mental health condition of the victim required to clarify a case and for the purposes of judicial proceedings.
